# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this repo is

An experiment comparing how well AI builds a three.js tropical beach scene. One shared base scene (water, sky, sand, light) with 8 prop slots, where only the prop source varies:

- **A**: procedural props written by codex.
- **B**: Tripo AI GLBs, decimated in Blender.
  - Exception: since 2026-10-20 the lifeguard tower is a Tripo image-to-model build (`tools/tripo_image_tower.py`) from a Codex reference image (`assets/raw/lifeguard_ladder/`) that adds a ladder and a railing opening. The text-prompt tower had no ladder. Blind scores and REPORT figures predate this swap.
- **C**: free library models (Poly Haven, Sketchfab, Poly Pizza).

On top of that there are an explore mode, a synced split-view compare page, a game mode, three characters (A/B/C), blind scoring, and comparison videos and slides.

Read these first:

- `PLAYBOOK.md`: the reusable process, commands and pitfalls.
- `NOTES.md`: per-feature implementation notes, written by codex.
- `REPORT.md` and `心得.md`: results.

User-facing docs are in Traditional Chinese (Taiwan); keep that.

Sibling worktrees `../beach3d-codex2` (port 5193) and `../beach3d-opus` (port 5192) hold the same pipeline re-run by other models (branches `codex2-run`, `opus-run`). They share only `assets/props.json` and the recorder hooks below.

## Commands

```sh
npx vite --port 5191 --strictPort      # dev server (npm run dev); many scripts assume 5191
npm run build                          # 6 entries: index, scene, compare, props, game, tidepool → dist/ (copies assets/, report/)
node scripts/shoot.mjs <A|B|C>         # fixed-camera stills → shots/<g>/{wide,beach,closeup}.png (SwiftShader)
node scripts/shoot-props.mjs <g> [slot]   # solo prop renders → shots/<g>/props/
node scripts/verify-game.mjs           # full game regression (quests, tide pool, open sea, boat, A/B/C, mobile, missing GLBs)
node scripts/verify-tidepool.mjs       # tide-pool page A/B/C: lift stones, observe 6, mobile → shots/tidepool/
node scripts/verify-explore.mjs        # explore-mode regression
node scripts/probe-extras.mjs [groups]             # game extras close-ups (castle, kite, crab, bird) → shots/extras/
node scripts/shoot-ui.mjs <mobile|desktop> <outdir> [group]   # game HUD states (start, shell, tower, tide pool, boat, pause, complete) → seg-1..7.png for UI review
node scripts/probe-clip.mjs [actions] [groups]   # clipping audit: rest,tower,boat,shell,ball × A/B/C (SNAP=1 stills → shots/clip/, DETAIL=1 surfaces)
node scripts/shoot-water.mjs [outdir] [time]      # water close-ups (surf, shallow, sun, far, swash) → shots/water/ for shading work
node scripts/probe-dive.mjs [groups] [gpu]       # dive from the boat: entry, deep, Snell's window, rise, back → shots/dive/
node scripts/probe-ball.mjs [groups]             # ball physics: rest drift, kick travel per power, walk-into push
node scripts/probe-carry.mjs [groups]            # coconuts: pick up, carry, throw, set down, float → shots/carry/
node scripts/probe-kick.mjs [groups] [outdir]   # ball kick side view at fixed ages + contact sheet → shots/kick/ (VIEW=front, POWER=<s held>)
node scripts/probe-legs.mjs [groups] [outdir]   # legs through a kick and a coconut throw, side and rear → shots/legs/
node scripts/probe-gait.mjs [groups] [outdir]   # walk/run width against the centre line + stills from in front → shots/gait/
node scripts/probe-impact.mjs [groups]          # kick hit-stop and camera shake against ?impact=0: frames held, camera turn, ball travel (POWER=<s held>)
node scripts/probe-reach.mjs [groups]           # interaction prompts from every side and at a distance, walk-up pick-ups and kicks, stick-to-run on touch → shots/reach/
node scripts/probe-climb.mjs [groups] [outdir]  # top of the tower climb: ladder data, hand heights and gaps, side stills + contact sheet → shots/climb/ (CLOSE=1 hand close-ups, NO_RAILS=1 pretends there are no uprights, DT, N)
```

Media pipeline:

- `node scripts/record-path.mjs <g> [fps] [path.json] [outdir]`: frame-by-frame GPU render along a camera path. Uses `SCENE_URL` and `SETTLE_MS` to point at other ports.
- `scripts/record-game.mjs` and `scripts/record-walk.mjs <g>`: game and character recordings.
- `node scripts/record-tidepool.mjs <g> [fps]` → `video/frames/tidepool_<g>/`, then `python3 tools/make_tidepool.py` → `video/tidepool_abc.mp4` (A/B/C side by side, same action timeline).
- `node scripts/record-game-tidepool.mjs [g]` → `video/game_tidepool.mp4` (walk to the pool in the game, observe all 6, return).
- `node scripts/record-game-opensea.mjs <g>` → `video/frames/opensea_<g>/`, `video/game_opensea_<g>.mp4` and `video/opensea_<g>.json` (observation times). Same boat and camera path for every group: row to 10 m from the buoy, turn once in place, press E when a prompt shows (at least 2.5 s apart). `DRY=1` only simulates. Then `python3 tools/make_opensea.py` → `video/opensea_abc.mp4`. The slides use re-encoded copies (crf 27) in `slides/assets/`.
- Compositing: `python3 tools/make_video.py`, `tools/make_zoom.py`, `tools/compare_models.py`.

Assets and stats:

- `.venv/bin/python tools/tripo_gen.py --dry-run|<slots>|--recover <task> <slot>`: Tripo generation. Spends credits, so ask the user first.
- `tools/decimate_all.sh`: Blender headless decimation to 30k tris.
- `tools/build_stats.py` → `report/stats.json`; `tools/compare.py` → `compare/*.png`.

Blind scoring:

- `tools/blind_score.py`; set `BLIND_CONFIG` to compare other dirs.
- `tools/blind_props.py`; `tools/judge_opus.py` runs Opus as a second judge.

Slides:

- `tools/build_live.sh` packages the three versions into `slides/live/`.
- `cd slides && python3 start.py` serves the slides and live demos (`live/`) on port 8730.

Delegation to other models:

- `tools/codex_run.sh <group> <step> <BRIEF.md>`: runs codex exec on a brief, timed via `tools/timed.sh` into `timing.csv`.
- Opus runs use `tools/claude_run.sh` in the opus worktree.

There is no lint or unit-test setup. Verification means running the Playwright scripts and looking at the screenshots.

## Architecture

- **One scene module, many pages.** `src/main.js` builds the renderer, sky, sand, water (`src/water.js`), coast details and the prop root for every page. It switches behaviour by URL and pathname:
  - `?cam=` gives a fixed view.
  - `?explore=1` lazy-loads `src/explore.js`.
  - `compare.html` adds `src/compare.js`, which uses one renderer with scissor viewports and toggles props per pane.
  - `game.html` adds `src/game/*`.
  - `props.html` runs `src/props-solo.js`, a separate solo viewer.
  - `tidepool.html` runs `src/tidepool/`, its own small scene that does not import `src/main.js`.
  - `index.html` is the hub (`src/hub.js`, reads `report/stats.json`).
- **Props.** `assets/props.json` is the single source of slots: `pos`, `height`, optional `maxLen`, `prompt`, and `paths.B/C` GLB paths. `src/props.js` `loadProps(group)` places either A's procedural builders (`src/props-a.js`) or GLBs.
  - `?swapB=<slot>:<glb path>` swaps one B prop for a trial, without touching `props.json` (same fit rule).
  - The fit rule is shared by all groups: `scale = min(height/size.y, maxLen/max(size.x,size.z))`. Don't change it per group, or the comparison stops being fair.
  - Grounding (since 2026-10-21, all groups): after the box bottom is put on the sand under the slot, `settle()` shifts the prop so the median gap of its lowest 6 cm of vertices to the sand is zero (on the slope the seaward side used to float up to ~15 cm). `node scripts/probe-ground.mjs [groups]` prints min/median/max gaps per prop.
- **Terrain and water are analytic and stateless.**
  - `src/terrain.js` `shore(x)` and `groundHeight(x,z)` are used by JS, by the shaders (`shoreGLSL`), by explore and game collision, and by the recorders.
  - `src/water.js` also exports CPU mirrors `sampleWater()` and `swashReach()`, which drive game buoyancy and footprints.
  - Shading-only wave detail (since 2026-10-21, same for all groups; blind scores and REPORT predate it): `swellState()` in the water fragment shader re-evaluates the four Gerstner waves per pixel (the offshore mesh is too coarse), for light through the swell (green-blue, most when backlit) and whitecaps where the crest is squeezed tightest (Jacobian), in patches, with foam left behind for a moment. The game's rowboat feeds `wakeRings` (24 stern points: x, z, time, speed; `WAKE_RINGS`): each spreads a ring of small ripples at a third of the boat's speed, which together keep the Kelvin wake's V; shading only, the surface does not move, so the CPU mirrors are unchanged.
  - Shallow water is see-through (since 2026-10-22, all groups): the water material is transparent with premultiplied alpha; up to about 1.6 m deep it writes only its own light (tint, caustics, reflection, foam) and lets the real sand and whatever stands in it (legs, the ball, a hull) through, tinted, 85% at most. Deeper it is opaque as before, except over the open-sea animals, which show through by the water's thickness in front of them (see Open sea below).
  - Borrowed from Ultra-Water (github.com/Humpalumps/Ultra-Water, MIT; ideas only, no code copied; since 2026-10-30, all groups; blind scores and REPORT predate it). Everything stays a function of position and the water clock (`verify-water` seeks 4 → 6 → 4 pixel-exact):
    - Sun on the water: a Beckmann lobe (`sunLobe()`, peak matched to the old Blinn 420) widened by the slope variance `fineSlope()` fades out with distance (`lostSlope()`, LEAN-style) and by `fwidth(N)` (specular AA), plus glints: hashed world cells about a pixel or two across, each a small round spot shining in a 0.16 s window, crossfaded to the next (`twinkle`), carrying part of the energy in a wider lobe.
    - Caustics: an area ratio of the refracted sunlight (`causticAt()` in `coastalGLSL`: the Jacobian of a ripple slope field `causticSlope()` times the still-water depth, folding into bright lines), drawn on the sand itself (`shadeSand()` takes the sun uniform now), so the shallows show them through the water and a diver sees them on the seabed. Sand under standing water is matte (no sun highlight from below).
    - Shore waves: the phase is ω times the closed-form shallow-water travel time over the analytic slope (`surfTravel()`, speed scaled by .65 so mid-surf spacing is unchanged; `surfK()` its rate), so crests slow, bunch and steepen to the sand; height by Green's law capped by breaking (`surfAmp()`). The JS mirror (`waterField`) uses the same functions; `swashReach()` is unchanged (travel time 0 at the waterline). Peeling: each crest breaks at its own distance out, varying along the beach and per wave (`breakAt`, foam only).
    - Foam: crest whitewater billows (`foamBillow()`) carried at the bore speed by a two-phase flow (restarts every 1.6 s, crossfaded), worn away with age (the time since the crest passed): solid, then holes, then lace; billow slopes shade creases, thin foam takes the water's tint and glows when backlit.
    - Sea rings are dispersive (Cauchy–Poisson): long waves lead, shorter ones trail; `sea.swell()` uses the same phase.
  - Diving (since 2026-10-30, game only, an extra: the seven quests are unchanged). From the boat at rest (under 1.5 m/s) over water deeper than 3 m, Q or the touch 潛水 button slips the rower over the side (`startDive()`, mode `dive`); W / the stick swims where the camera looks (pitch included, `explore` now exposes `pitch` and `input().up`), Space / 上浮 rises, a little buoyancy towards 1 m down when idle; kept in open water (`landHeight` under -1.2 m), over the seabed and under the surface. The body lies along the swim direction (root at the feet, placed so the middle is on the diver), the walk clip as the flutter kick, hands reaching ahead by IK. The camera follows behind and is clamped 0.3 m under the surface (no half-in view). E within 3.5 m of the boat climbs back (`endDive()`); the boat keeps floating meanwhile (`floatBoat()`). Under the surface: the water is double-sided and its shader draws Snell's window from below (sky through the ~48.6° circle with the sun, total internal reflection outside, foam dark against it); `src/game/underwater.js` turns the scene fog blue-green and thicker with depth, filters and dims the lights, hides the sky dome, adds sun shafts along the refracted sun (hashed 3 m cells round the camera, faded near the eye) and marine snow (points wrapping a 14 m box). Hooks (auto): `__GAME__.dive()`, `surface()`, `diver`. `verify-game` dives at the buoy and climbs back (shot `dive.png`).
    - Seabed (`src/game/seabed.js`, since 2026-10-30): five reef patches (`PATCHES`, four on the way out from the dock, a big one round the buoy) with rocks, corals (branching, brain, fan; each instance tinted from `CORAL_TINTS`), seaweed swaying in a vertex shader, and five tropical fish (`FISH`): schools of yellow tangs and blue tangs circling the patch, clownfish, butterflyfish and angelfish each looping round a coral head; fish within 2.5 m of the diver dart away (eased state, the only one). Placement, counts, sizes and motion are seeded and shared by all groups; everything glows at a quarter of its albedo so colours survive the underwater light. Models: A procedural (`buildA()`, `fishGeometry()`), C `assets/seabed/C/<id>.glb` (Poly Pizza / Sketchfab, `CREDITS.md`, `src/credits.js` section 潛水：海底), B `assets/seabed/B/<id>.glb` (Tripo text-to-model, `tools/tripo_seabed.py`, 10 × 20 credits on 2026-10-30, logged in `assets/tripo/log.csv` as `seabed:<id>`; decimated to 3000 tris, fish 2000, fish head +X by `z-90`, the yellow tang `z90`); a missing GLB falls back to A per id. GLBs are normalised at load by A's rule (`loadGlb()`: fish length 1, the rest base at 0 and largest extent 1). Drawn only while the camera is under water. While diving, sea animals within 45 m of the diver swim deeper (`sea.setDiver()`, about 1 m plus a quarter of their length, eased). `probe-dive` adds `reef`, `fish` and `buoy` shots; `__GAME__.diveTo(x,z,above)` and `__GAME__.seabed` (auto).
  - Wading (`src/explore.js`, game and explore alike): while the walker stands in water, the feet in turn feed `wadeRings` (10 points: x, z, time, strength; `WADE_RINGS`): short ripples (about 35 cm) running out at walking pace and a broken foam ring, gone within a couple of seconds; shading only. They replaced flat white ring meshes fixed at y 0.09.
  - All animation must derive from one time value so offline rendering is deterministic.
- **Determinism and automation hooks.** These are what the recorders and verifiers use; keep them working.
  - `window.__SCENE__` (`{scene, camera, renderer, water, …}`) and `window.__READY__`.
  - `window.__TIME__`: when set, it overrides the water/sand clock.
  - `?time=N`: freezes time.
  - With `?auto=1` only: `window.__EXPLORE__` and `window.__GAME__` (including deterministic `step(seconds)`, `teleport`, `view`, `interact`).
  - In game mode, game/explore dt is derived from the water clock, so a frozen clock freezes play. `__GAME__.step()` records the time it advanced to (`water.userData.simTime`), and the frame loop only simulates past it; before 2026-10-21 a recorder that stepped and then waited for a frame advanced play twice per step (game recordings ran at double speed).
- **Characters.** `src/game/character.js` serves both the game and the solo viewer.
  - A: procedural SkinnedMesh.
  - B: Tripo `assets/character/{idle,walk,run,jump,climb}.glb`, with clips merged onto one skeleton. Since 2026-10-20 the rig is Tripo v3.0 `spec=unity` (67 joints, three-joint fingers). It was re-rigged from the original model task with `tools/tripo_rig_test.py` and `tools/tripo_retarget_v3.py`; credits are in `assets/tripo/log.csv`. The old 41-joint rig had no fingers.
  - C: Quaternius `assets/character_C/character.glb`.
  - Missing clip poses (sit, lie, paddle, climb) are procedural bone aiming.
  - Gotcha: an `update(0)` call must not `restore()` bones. three.js `PropertyMixer` skips writing unchanged values, so the rest pose would stay on screen in offline recordings.
  - Walk/run playback is time-scaled to measured clip stride so feet don't slide.
  - IK layer (`solve()` in `character.js`, all three rigs): analytic two-bone IK for hands/feet with world targets and per-limb weights, pelvis drop for crouches, terrain-following feet (`ground`), spine lean/twist, head look-at, wrist aim (`handAim`) and finger curl (`curl`). The game passes targets per mode from `poseIK()` in `src/game/index.js`; `info().ik` reports reach errors.
  - Grip (`curl`): rigs with finger bones (B) bend each finger joint about an axis built in bind space (T pose, palms down). A rig without fingers instead gets a knuckle bone and a thumb bone per hand at load, re-skinned in bind space from vertices wholly on the hand. Wrist aim puts the roll on the forearm; a wrist that rolls far tears the skin. The Tripo climb clip is a chest-to-wall climb: at load its hips are pinned at the standing position and its hips-to-head rotations at the bind pose (values overwritten in place, since the actions already exist), so the game's body placement and `spine.lean` set the torso. On a leaning ladder `climbPose` keeps the hips about 42 cm off the ladder plane (nearly over the feet, as on steep stairs) and 25 cm below the rung line, so both knees bend. Past the top rung a hand moves to a hold (`topHold()` in `climbPose`), since 2026-11-04: `ladder.handrails` (own ladders) lists, per side, the nearest upright beside the centre line, found by sideways probes. Into an opening (B) the palms go flat on the deck a little in from the edge (no grip, the torso leaning in), then on getting up to those uprights at about waist height on the deck; going over a railing (A, `over` above the deck) the deck edge is blocked, so the hands take the uprights above the deck straight away, never above where they end. Fingers round the upright towards the tower, palm against its inner face; with no upright the hands stay flat and let go earlier. The hands let go as the hips pass the uprights (`m` .5–.72) and the climb clip ends just after (`onLadder`, m < .62), or the arm swung out in the clip's pose. C climbs stairs and is unchanged.
  - Launch: E at the beached boat swaps in the clone exactly where and how the prop lies (`boat.restYaw`); holding W pushes it from the stern (hands on the stern top found by scanning the centre line, lean eased where it rides high), first swinging it round on the spot if it faces up the beach, then down to the water past the umbrella and driftwood (hull corners against the prop boxes). It rests on the sand (keel on the ground) or floats, whichever is higher. Where its middle is deep enough to row (ground < -0.75 m) the rower climbs in over the stern (`boardPose()`, 3.2 s, a function of the time since it began; keys in vessel space): steps up to the stern and takes its top in both hands, pushes up with the chest folded over it (hips at the top), brings one knee then the other over (each foot on a Bézier through a point 26 cm above the top) onto what is inside (`boat.deck`: floor or thwart along the centre line, probed at hull setup), crouches with the hands on the gunwales (`boat.deck[].gun`: the side found by a ray from outside, hits over 0.9 m off the centre line skipped for C's oars), steps forward over the thwart and lowers onto it facing the bow while the hands go to the paddle. The weight presses the stern down 5° and settles the hull 2 cm. At 2.9 s the hips are on the seat and the seated pose takes over with `character.update({snapPose:true})` (body offset not blended, so no jump); `character.hipHeight` is exposed for this. With `?auto=1`, `__GAME__.boardInfo()` returns the stern, deck profile and current targets. Holding S pulls it back (0.9 m/s, walking backwards: a negative `speed` to `character.update()` runs the gait phase the other way), A / D swinging it, so a hull run into a lounger can be backed off; `verify-game` checks it. E during the push skips to the old start at the dock (the paddle, hidden while pushing, is shown again; `verify-game` checks it). With `?auto=1` it is off unless `__GAME__.pushBoat=true` (probes and recorders board directly); `__GAME__.launch` reports it. `verify-game` covers it (shot `push.png`).
  - Splashes (`src/game/splash.js`): a blade crossing the water line (in or out) and, under way, both sides of the bow emit a splash event; drops and a speckled foam ring are a pure function of the time since the event. Paddle length and roll come from the hull: at the bottom of the stroke the blade is 16 cm under the water and 45 cm clear of the side (a blade dipped beside the hull read as spray from the boat). While a blade is in the water it leaves small swirls every 0.08 s. Drops are camera-facing quads stretched along their velocity (a streak, not a bead), leaving from across the blade's width; bigger splashes add a dim mist puff; a blade just out of the water drips for 0.8 s (drip events: three falling drops and a small ring where they land). Quad winding: the side vector must be `(dir.y,-dir.x)` or the quads are back-face culled. Splash heights use `surfaceHeight()`.
  - Wake and hull foam (`src/game/wake.js`): the stern is sampled every 0.15 s while under way; the wake is a foam ribbon over those samples that widens at about the Kelvin angle (capped at 1.2 m/s), breaks up and fades over 5.5 s, and is hidden over sand. Both it and the hull foam line count as in the water only where the swash reaches (`wet()`: `z-shore(x)<swashReach(x,t)` and 10 cm deep), since the water mesh runs on over the dry beach; a boat pushed over the sand used to wear its foam line there. A foam line hugs the hull at the water line (outline probed inward at local y 0 when the hull is set up), wider at the bow under way. Foam texture is fixed to the water (v along distance travelled, the ring in world space). Everything is a function of the samples and the time, so recordings stay deterministic. `surfaceHeight()` caches the displaced grid corners per time, so the hundreds of calls per frame stay under about 0.5 ms.
  - Boat: one stroke phase drives a double-bladed paddle, both hands (overhand grip), torso twist and thrust pulses. The hull is turned so its long axis runs along travel; the rower sits on a thwart near midships, feet braced on the floor.
  - Shells: walk up, face, squat (pelvis down, feet planted), reach; the shell counts when the hand closes on it and rides in the hand.
  - Interactions as definitions (since 2026-11-02): `src/game/actions.js` is one runner for the on-foot interactions (walk to a spot at 1.4 m/s and turn, hold to charge over `CHARGE.time` 1 s of game time with auto-fire `CHARGE.full` 0.4 s after full and tap < `CHARGE.tap` 0.18 s, events fired once at their age, per-frame step, end, `setHold` handed back) plus curve helpers (`ramp`, `pulse`, `bump`); `src/game/moves.js` holds the definitions (`setup`, `approach{face,within,avoid,walkYaw}`, `charge`, `tick`, `begin`, `events`, `step`, `duration`, `end`, `pose`): `PICKUP` (shells and coconuts), `KICK`, `TOSS` (coconut set-down / throw) and `SCOOP`. The code and numbers moved unchanged (probe-kick/probe-carry/probe-ball logs identical, stills pixel-identical). `index.js` keeps `pickup`/`kick`/`toss` as mirrors of the running action (`onChange`) for its many readers; `ctx.character` is a getter (the character is swapped on group change). `SCOOP` was added as a definition only, to show a new interaction needs no runner code: E on open dry sand with nothing to interact with crouches, scoops a handful in front, stands with it at the chest and lets it run out (puffs at the scoop and from the hand).

B/C clips are time-scaled to the measured clip speed (cap 5×). A's procedural gait matches its swing amplitude to speed. Footprints are stamped where a foot really comes down (`src/game/index.js`, since 2026-10-22): it has stopped moving across the sand (walking 0.08 s under 0.3 m/s; since 2026-11-01 the thresholds scale with the body's speed, so a running foot, down for about 0.1 s and still creeping, counts when under 30% of the pace for a frame) near the rig's lowest foot height, and must lift (8 cm higher or over 0.8 m/s, 60% of the pace when running) before it prints again; a foot shuffling under 15 cm does not print twice. So stops and settling steps print under the feet. (The old code read a `character.plants` flag that never existed and printed every 0.55 m beside the body's centre.)

## Conventions and gotchas

- Headless GPU screenshots of the tide pool occasionally capture a frame without the water layer; re-rendering the same time fixes it. The tide-pool recorders shoot each frame until two screenshots match. Also scan finished frames for single-frame spikes.
- Blender MCP library toggles (Sketchfab, Poly Pizza) are per scene: a new temp scene starts with them off.
- Headless Chromium path: `~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1243/chrome-linux64/chrome`.
  - GPU: `--use-gl=angle --use-angle=gl-egl` (≈0.17 s/frame).
  - SwiftShader: `--use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader` (≈1.6 s/frame), used for stills and verification.
- Codex runs stop the Vite dev server when they exit. Restart it before recording.
- When writing briefs for codex, state the "must not change" list explicitly: water look, fit rule, `props.json`, camera presets, the hooks above, and port 5191.
- Before a long video render, preview at 0.5–2 fps and look at a contact sheet. This catches cameras clipping through props and black frames.
- Comparisons must stay fair:
  - Same camera path, same time, same framing.
  - Blind scoring anonymizes and rotates order.
  - Framing differences between sources bias scores; normalize them (`tools/blind_props.py` `fit()`).
- `.env` (Tripo key) is gitignored. `assets/raw/`, trial GLBs (`*__*.glb`), `video/*.mp4` and `video/frames/` are not committed.
- Commit messages are in Chinese.
- Paths are relative so the build works under a sub-path (GitHub Pages `ammosu.github.io/beach3d-eval/`): Vite `base:'./'`, page links without a leading `/`, and runtime asset URLs through `asset()` in `src/url.js` (it strips the leading `/` of `props.json` paths, which must not change). The build's asset copy skips `assets/raw/` and trial `*__*.glb`.
- Publishing: `.github/workflows/pages.yml` deploys `slides/` (slides at the root, `live/{main,codex2,opus}/` from `tools/build_live.sh`, which builds with `--base ./` and rewrites the sibling versions' hard-coded `/assets/` in their bundles) on every push to `master` that touches `slides/`. CI does not rebuild: run `tools/build_live.sh` and commit `slides/live/`. `slides/start.py` now serves only port 8730.
- Credits: group C's third-party models (mostly CC BY) are credited in the page by a 「素材出處」 button (`src/credits.js`, same data as the `CREDITS.md` files; keep them in step), shown only where C is on screen: hub C card, explore/game HUD and start/pause panel (pointer lock leaves no cursor while playing), the C compare pane, props viewer, tide pool. item.aggregated_output:
116-  - With `?auto=1` only: `window.__EXPLORE__` and `window.__GAME__` (including deterministic `step(seconds)`, `teleport`, `view`, `interact`).
117-  - In game mode, game/explore dt is derived from the water clock, so a frozen clock freezes play. `__GAME__.step()` records the time it advanced to (`water.userData.simTime`), and the frame loop only simulates past it; before 2026-10-21 a recorder that stepped and then waited for a frame advanced play twice per step (game recordings ran at double speed).
118:- **Characters.** `src/game/character.js` serves both the game and the solo viewer.
119-  - A: procedural SkinnedMesh.
120-  - B: Tripo `assets/character/{idle,walk,run,jump,climb}.glb`, with clips merged onto one skeleton. Since 2026-10-20 the rig is Tripo v3.0 `spec=unity` (67 joints, three-joint fingers). It was re-rigged from the original model task with `tools/tripo_rig_test.py` and `tools/tripo_retarget_v3.py`; credits are in `assets/tripo/log.csv`. The old 41-joint rig had no fingers.
121-  - C: Quaternius `assets/character_C/character.glb`.
122-  - Missing clip poses (sit, lie, paddle, climb) are procedural bone aiming.
123-  - Gotcha: an `update(0)` call must not `restore()` bones. three.js `PropertyMixer` skips writing unchanged values, so the rest pose would stay on screen in offline recordings.
124-  - Walk/run playback is time-scaled to measured clip stride so feet don't slide.
125-  - IK layer (`solve()` in `character.js`, all three rigs): analytic two-bone IK for hands/feet with world targets and per-limb weights, pelvis drop for crouches, terrain-following feet (`ground`), spine lean/twist, head look-at, wrist aim (`handAim`) and finger curl (`curl`). The game passes targets per mode from `poseIK()` in `src/game/index.js`; `info().ik` reports reach errors.
126-  - Grip (`curl`): rigs with finger bones (B) bend each finger joint about an axis built in bind space (T pose, palms down). A rig without fingers instead gets a knuckle bone and a thumb bone per hand at load, re-skinned in bind space from vertices wholly on the hand. Wrist aim puts the roll on the forearm; a wrist that rolls far tears the skin. The Tripo climb clip is a chest-to-wall climb: at load its hips are pinned at the standing position and its hips-to-head rotations at the bind pose (values overwritten in place, since the actions already exist), so the game's body placement and `spine.lean` set the torso. On a leaning ladder `climbPose` keeps the hips about 42 cm off the ladder plane (nearly over the feet, as on steep stairs) and 25 cm below the rung line, so both knees bend. Past the top rung a hand moves to a hold (`topHold()` in `climbPose`), since 2026-11-04: `ladder.handrails` (own ladders) lists, per side, the nearest upright beside the centre line, found by sideways probes. Into an opening (B) the palms go flat on the deck a little in from the edge (no grip, the torso leaning in), then on getting up to those uprights at about waist height on the deck; going over a railing (A, `over` above the deck) the deck edge is blocked, so the hands take the uprights above the deck straight away, never above where they end. Fingers round the upright towards the tower, palm against its inner face; with no upright the hands stay flat and let go earlier. The hands let go as the hips pass the uprights (`m` .5–.72) and the climb clip ends just after (`onLadder`, m < .62), or the arm swung out in the clip's pose. C climbs stairs and is unchanged.
127-  - Launch: E at the beached boat swaps in the clone exactly where and how the prop lies (`boat.restYaw`); holding W pushes it from the stern (hands on the stern top found by scanning the centre line, lean eased where it rides high), first swinging it round on the spot if it faces up the beach, then down to the water past the umbrella and driftwood (hull corners against the prop boxes). It rests on the sand (keel on the ground) or floats, whichever is higher. Where its middle is deep enough to row (ground < -0.75 m) the rower climbs in over the stern (`boardPose()`, 3.2 s, a function of the time since it began; keys in vessel space): steps up to the stern and takes its top in both hands, pushes up with the chest folded over it (hips at the top), brings one knee then the other over (each foot on a Bézier through a point 26 cm above the top) onto what is inside (`boat.deck`: floor or thwart along the centre line, probed at hull setup), crouches with the hands on the gunwales (`boat.deck[].gun`: the side found by a ray from outside, hits over 0.9 m off the centre line skipped for C's oars), steps forward over the thwart and lowers onto it facing the bow while the hands go to the paddle. The weight presses the stern down 5° and settles the hull 2 cm. At 2.9 s the hips are on the seat and the seated pose takes over with `character.update({snapPose:true})` (body offset not blended, so no jump); `character.hipHeight` is exposed for this. With `?auto=1`, `__GAME__.boardInfo()` returns the stern, deck profile and current targets. Holding S pulls it back (0.9 m/s, walking backwards: a negative `speed` to `character.update()` runs the gait phase the other way), A / D swinging it, so a hull run into a lounger can be backed off; `verify-game` checks it. E during the push skips to the old start at the dock (the paddle, hidden while pushing, is shown again; `verify-game` checks it). With `?auto=1` it is off unless `__GAME__.pushBoat=true` (probes and recorders board directly); `__GAME__.launch` reports it. `verify-game` covers it (shot `push.png`).
128-  - Splashes (`src/game/splash.js`): a blade crossing the water line (in or out) and, under way, both sides of the bow emit a splash event; drops and a speckled foam ring are a pure function of the time since the event. Paddle length and roll come from the hull: at the bottom of the stroke the blade is 16 cm under the water and 45 cm clear of the side (a blade dipped beside the hull read as spray from the boat). While a blade is in the water it leaves small swirls every 0.08 s. Drops are camera-facing quads stretched along their velocity (a streak, not a bead), leaving from across the blade's width; bigger splashes add a dim mist puff; a blade just out of the water drips for 0.8 s (drip events: three falling drops and a small ring where they land). Quad winding: the side vector must be `(dir.y,-dir.x)` or the quads are back-face culled. Splash heights use `surfaceHeight()`.
129-  - Wake and hull foam (`src/game/wake.js`): the stern is sampled every 0.15 s while under way; the wake is a foam ribbon over those samples that widens at about the Kelvin angle (capped at 1.2 m/s), breaks up and fades over 5.5 s, and is hidden over sand. Both it and the hull foam line count as in the water only where the swash reaches (`wet()`: `z-shore(x)<swashReach(x,t)` and 10 cm deep), since the water mesh runs on over the dry beach; a boat pushed over the sand used to wear its foam line there. A foam line hugs the hull at the water line (outline probed inward at local y 0 when the hull is set up), wider at the bow under way. Foam texture is fixed to the water (v along distance travelled, the ring in world space). Everything is a function of the samples and the time, so recordings stay deterministic. `surfaceHeight()` caches the displaced grid corners per time, so the hundreds of calls per frame stay under about 0.5 ms.
130-  - Boat: one stroke phase drives a double-bladed paddle, both hands (overhand grip), torso twist and thrust pulses. The hull is turned so its long axis runs along travel; the rower sits on a thwart near midships, feet braced on the floor.
131-  - Shells: walk up, face, squat (pelvis down, feet planted), reach; the shell counts when the hand closes on it and rides in the hand.
132-  - Interactions as definitions (since 2026-11-02): `src/game/actions.js` is one runner for the on-foot interactions (walk to a spot at 1.4 m/s and turn, hold to charge over `CHARGE.time` 1 s of game time with auto-fire `CHARGE.full` 0.4 s after full and tap < `CHARGE.tap` 0.18 s, events fired once at their age, per-frame step, end, `setHold` handed back) plus curve helpers (`ramp`, `pulse`, `bump`); `src/game/moves.js` holds the definitions (`setup`, `approach{face,within,avoid,walkYaw}`, `charge`, `tick`, `begin`, `events`, `step`, `duration`, `end`, `pose`): `PICKUP` (shells and coconuts), `KICK`, `TOSS` (coconut set-down / throw) and `SCOOP`. The code and numbers moved unchanged (probe-kick/probe-carry/probe-ball logs identical, stills pixel-identical). `index.js` keeps `pickup`/`kick`/`toss` as mirrors of the running action (`onChange`) for its many readers; `ctx.character` is a getter (the character is swapped on group change). `SCOOP` was added as a definition only, to show a new interaction needs no runner code: E on open dry sand with nothing to interact with crouches, scoops a handful in front, stands with it at the chest and lets it run out (puffs at the scoop and from the hand).
133-  - Impact (`src/game/impact.js`, since 2026-11-02, all groups alike, the kick only so far): a hit-stop (on-foot game time at 3% for 20–120 ms by power, 50 ms back up; the physics world takes no time while held, the water and the camera carry on) and a camera shake (rotation only, after the camera is placed, about 1° at full power, 0.1° for a tap, gone in 0.38 s; off with `prefers-reduced-motion`). Both are functions of the time since the hit on the water clock. `?impact=0` turns both off; the ball's travel is unchanged. A kick now ends up to 0.17 s later in clock time, so waiting on `kick.age` is safer than stepping a fixed time. `scripts/record-impact.mjs [group]` records on/off frames for a side-by-side.
134-  - Ball (since 2026-10-22, reworked 2026-11-01 after soccer-kick mocap such as CMU subject 10): a shot, not a clip. Charge and aim (since 2026-11-01): E held (keydown/keyup; the touch button by pointerdown/up) charges over 1 s of game time (`KICK_CHARGE`, water clock), a tap is power 0 (a light touch, 3.5 m/s along the sand), full is a lofted shot (14 m/s, 4.2 up; `ball.kick(player,dir,power)`); it fires once at the spot with the key up, or by itself 0.4 s after full. The kick goes where the camera looks (`explore.yaw`) when the ball is within 75° of that, else player → ball; the spot follows the aim until the wind-up, and the walk there circles the ball at 1.12 m (`KICK_CLEAR`) so it is never shoved; the ball is not pushed by the body during a kick. While charging at the spot the body sinks and leans over the ball; a bar over the head shows the charge (`#kick-charge`). Power also scales the backswing and follow-through. Soles (since 2026-11-02): the plant foot lands heel first, rolls flat, its heel rises as the body passes and it steps up to the idle stance by 1.03 s (it used to slide there in the last 0.15 s); the kicking foot's toes point through the swing. # CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this repo is

An experiment comparing how well AI builds a three.js tropical beach scene. One shared base scene (water, sky, sand, light) with 8 prop slots, where only the prop source varies:

- **A**: procedural props written by codex.
- **B**: Tripo AI GLBs, decimated in Blender.
  - Exception: since 2026-10-20 the lifeguard tower is a Tripo image-to-model build (`tools/tripo_image_tower.py`) from a Codex reference image (`assets/raw/lifeguard_ladder/`) that adds a ladder and a railing opening. The text-prompt tower had no ladder. Blind scores and REPORT figures predate this swap.
- **C**: free library models (Poly Haven, Sketchfab, Poly Pizza).

On top of that there are an explore mode, a synced split-view compare page, a game mode, three characters (A/B/C), blind scoring, and comparison videos and slides.

Read these first:

- `PLAYBOOK.md`: the reusable process, commands and pitfalls.
- `NOTES.md`: per-feature implementation notes, written by codex.
- `REPORT.md` and `心得.md`: results.

User-facing docs are in Traditional Chinese (Taiwan); keep that.

Sibling worktrees `../beach3d-codex2` (port 5193) and `../beach3d-opus` (port 5192) hold the same pipeline re-run by other models (branches `codex2-run`, `opus-run`). They share only `assets/props.json` and the recorder hooks below.

## Commands

```sh
npx vite --port 5191 --strictPort      # dev server (npm run dev); many scripts assume 5191
npm run build                          # 6 entries: index, scene, compare, props, game, tidepool → dist/ (copies assets/, report/)
node scripts/shoot.mjs <A|B|C>         # fixed-camera stills → shots/<g>/{wide,beach,closeup}.png (SwiftShader)
node scripts/shoot-props.mjs <g> [slot]   # solo prop renders → shots/<g>/props/
node scripts/verify-game.mjs           # full game regression (quests, tide pool, open sea, boat, A/B/C, mobile, missing GLBs)
node scripts/verify-tidepool.mjs       # tide-pool page A/B/C: lift stones, observe 6, mobile → shots/tidepool/
node scripts/verify-explore.mjs        # explore-mode regression
node scripts/probe-extras.mjs [groups]             # game extras close-ups (castle, kite, crab, bird) → shots/extras/
node scripts/shoot-ui.mjs <mobile|desktop> <outdir> [group]   # game HUD states (start, shell, tower, tide pool, boat, pause, complete) → seg-1..7.png for UI review
node scripts/probe-clip.mjs [actions] [groups]   # clipping audit: rest,tower,boat,shell,ball × A/B/C (SNAP=1 stills → shots/clip/, DETAIL=1 surfaces)
node scripts/shoot-water.mjs [outdir] [time]      # water close-ups (surf, shallow, sun, far, swash) → shots/water/ for shading work
node scripts/probe-dive.mjs [groups] [gpu]       # dive from the boat: entry, deep, Snell's window, rise, back → shots/dive/
node scripts/probe-ball.mjs [groups]             # ball physics: rest drift, kick travel per power, walk-into push
node scripts/probe-carry.mjs [groups]            # coconuts: pick up, carry, throw, set down, float → shots/carry/
node scripts/probe-kick.mjs [groups] [outdir]   # ball kick side view at fixed ages + contact sheet → shots/kick/ (VIEW=front, POWER=<s held>)
node scripts/probe-legs.mjs [groups] [outdir]   # legs through a kick and a coconut throw, side and rear → shots/legs/
node scripts/probe-gait.mjs [groups] [outdir]   # walk/run width against the centre line + stills from in front → shots/gait/
node scripts/probe-impact.mjs [groups]          # kick hit-stop and camera shake against ?impact=0: frames held, camera turn, ball travel (POWER=<s held>)
node scripts/probe-reach.mjs [groups]           # interaction prompts from every side and at a distance, walk-up pick-ups and kicks, stick-to-run on touch → shots/reach/
node scripts/probe-climb.mjs [groups] [outdir]  # top of the tower climb: ladder data, hand heights and gaps, side stills + contact sheet → shots/climb/ (CLOSE=1 hand close-ups, NO_RAILS=1 pretends there are no uprights, DT, N)
```

Media pipeline:

- `node scripts/record-path.mjs <g> [fps] [path.json] [outdir]`: frame-by-frame GPU render along a camera path. Uses `SCENE_URL` and `SETTLE_MS` to point at other ports.
- `scripts/record-game.mjs` and `scripts/record-walk.mjs <g>`: game and character recordings.
- `node scripts/record-tidepool.mjs <g> [fps]` → `video/frames/tidepool_<g>/`, then `python3 tools/make_tidepool.py` → `video/tidepool_abc.mp4` (A/B/C side by side, same action timeline).
- `node scripts/record-game-tidepool.mjs [g]` → `video/game_tidepool.mp4` (walk to the pool in the game, observe all 6, return).
- `node scripts/record-game-opensea.mjs <g>` → `video/frames/opensea_<g>/`, `video/game_opensea_<g>.mp4` and `video/opensea_<g>.json` (observation times). Same boat and camera path for every group: row to 10 m from the buoy, turn once in place, press E when a prompt shows (at least 2.5 s apart). `DRY=1` only simulates. Then `python3 tools/make_opensea.py` → `video/opensea_abc.mp4`. The slides use re-encoded copies (crf 27) in `slides/assets/`.
- Compositing: `python3 tools/make_video.py`, `tools/make_zoom.py`, `tools/compare_models.py`.

Assets and stats:

- `.venv/bin/python tools/tripo_gen.py --dry-run|<slots>|--recover <task> <slot>`: Tripo generation. Spends credits, so ask the user first.
- `tools/decimate_all.sh`: Blender headless decimation to 30k tris.
- `tools/build_stats.py` → `report/stats.json`; `tools/compare.py` → `compare/*.png`.

Blind scoring:

- `tools/blind_score.py`; set `BLIND_CONFIG` to compare other dirs.
- `tools/blind_props.py`; `tools/judge_opus.py` runs Opus as a second judge.

Slides:

- `tools/build_live.sh` packages the three versions into `slides/live/`.
- `cd slides && python3 start.py` serves the slides and live demos (`live/`) on port 8730.

Delegation to other models:

- `tools/codex_run.sh <group> <step> <BRIEF.md>`: runs codex exec on a brief, timed via `tools/timed.sh` into `timing.csv`.
- Opus runs use `tools/claude_run.sh` in the opus worktree.

There is no lint or unit-test setup. Verification means running the Playwright scripts and looking at the screenshots.

## Architecture

- **One scene module, many pages.** `src/main.js` builds the renderer, sky, sand, water (`src/water.js`), coast details and the prop root for every page. It switches behaviour by URL and pathname:
